title: Pyramid — executable, bounded and understandable development

intent.statement: Agents complete authorized development through safe decisions, actual candidate-bound checks, scoped context, precise replanning and isolated collaboration; engineers understand current results and risks; retained evidence and measured whole-workflow cost support trustworthy acceptance.

success_evidence.description: The public skill selects a dependency-safe next action, explains current blockers, and continues authorized independent work without routine approval loops.
Registered local procedures produce candidate-bound execution records; execution, semantic acceptance and actual visual review remain distinct, and false or stale success is rejected.
Role-scoped packets, bounded code retrieval and recoverable output preserve necessary decisions while reducing measured information-transfer overhead.
Current product behavior stays linked to stable requirements; create and scoped replan reuse existing procedures and preserve unaffected IDs, contracts and valid producer proof.
Task workers and read-only helpers use isolated candidates and resources; a coordinator rejects stale results, avoids duplicate review and verifies the integrated outcome.
Engineers use the existing Board, Flow and shared inspector to identify the next gate, blockers, evidence identity and limits without confusing historical acceptance with current eligibility.
A reference-aware inventory and guarded disposable-artifact procedure control growth without deleting canonical history, active/handoff proof, unresolved failures or uncertain resources.
Fixed representative real-host workloads establish correctness, actual usage, time, questions, rework, artifact growth and human decision accuracy; unavailable measurements remain unknown.

The system retains single canonical authority, compatibility, history, least authority and fail-closed transitions; no command, hook, plan or receipt grants host permission or guarantees semantic truth.

constraints: Target only the Standalone Pyramid Skill source in /Users/merdankiji/localGit/pyramid-task; local-canonical. Installed 4.1.0 is the current controller; local 4.2.0 source and completed Observer are observed baselines, not remote or installed qualification.
Preserve dirty source, completed Observer history, current baseline and existing contracts. Generate a candidate only; archive/reset requires approval of the exact preview.
Runtime policy stays deterministic; explicit process execution is isolated in an adapter. One guarded canonical publication boundary owns results.
Use existing project-fit tests/probes/browser harness first. One run may satisfy multiple criteria; do not duplicate testing by layer or task owner.

Agent commands list available verification entry points, not a mandatory rerun checklist. Use affected checks for component work; run the full regression suite at the final cumulative gate and after relevant regression-producing changes.
Retain scoped guards, producer-bound proof, dirty/untracked fingerprints and directional invalidation; unknown freshness/ownership fails closed.
Independent product work is not blocked by harness, host or release capability it does not consume. Acceptance remains blocked when required proof is absent.
Register cost/quality thresholds before comparing candidates; report actual input/cache/output separately and retain failed pairs. No fabricated savings or semantic quality from byte counts.
Capture and actually inspect rendered UI evidence where applicable; human comprehension is measured by humans, not an agent proxy.
Registered procedure/receipt/context is not host authorization or OS sandboxing. Respect enforced restrictions; cleanup of personal or uncertain resources is forbidden.
Current product specs reference canonical requirements but do not become a second mutable execution ledger. Existing schema/host compatibility is explicitly tested.
non_goals: No second canonical ledger or competing workflow controller.
No live installation, commit, push or deployment.
No permission escalation, personal-profile access or automatic cleanup.
No universal code index, model service or claimed full ASD-STE100 compliance.
No mandatory installation of Comet, OpenSpec, Superpowers, CodeGraph, RTK, Ponytail or Caveman.
No automatic native compaction, unsupported hooks or hosted AI task generation.
No arbitrary remote/privileged runner, production customer execution, general fleet/resource manager or whole-repository rewrite.

decisions.question: Which development system owns the work?
decisions.choice: Extend Standalone Pyramid with deterministic policy, explicit local runner adapters and project-fit agent guidance. Keep one canonical controller.
alternatives: Run Comet and Pyramid as competing authorities
Install every researched tool as a mandatory stack
decisions.rationale: Dual authority introduces reconciliation risk and mandatory tooling adds unmeasured setup/context cost. Adopt capabilities through bounded interfaces, not product names.

decisions.question: How is the complete intent demonstrated?
decisions.choice: Baseline: local 4.2.0 plus completed Board/Flow, installed 4.1 controller, uncommitted source and pending code binding. Accept three cumulative public journeys: OUTCOME-810 trustworthy repair; OUTCOME-820 repeated change with scoped context/specs/parallelism; OUTCOME-830 qualified agent-and-engineer full lifecycle.
alternatives: Seven isolated component gates without a public journey
Treat setup or a task wave as an accepted increment
decisions.rationale: Each rung is usable and resolves a different outcome-level risk. All agreed capabilities remain required. Later gates re-establish inherited behavior; implementation may proceed ahead when it does not consume earlier work. GATE-830 already covers every requirement, so no redundant final gate is added.

decisions.question: How do we preserve parallelism and truthful dependencies?
decisions.choice: CONTRACT-801 establishes consumed interface, assurance and measurement facts. Independent adapters/policy/context/specification/delegation/Observer/retention start afterward in the same earliest wave. Integration edges constrain acceptance without serializing independent coding. Core/CLI integrations have one sequential owner.
alternatives: Require every first-increment gate before all later coding
Let all workers edit core/CLI concurrently
decisions.rationale: Actual consumption and shared executable entry edits need dependencies; an unavailable final runner or review is not a start dependency for unrelated implementation. Live conflict/resource analysis still determines actual grouping.

decisions.question: What proof and cleanup authority is accepted?
decisions.choice: Separate execution provenance, source identity, semantic/visual judgment, actual host permission and independent reviewer provenance. Preserve old proof trust and failed evidence. Cleanup requires explicit bounded authority and positive ownership/reference/process checks.
alternatives: Trust a manually submitted passed receipt
Treat any hash as independent execution proof
decisions.rationale: Local instrumentation is not a security oracle against a malicious process. Unknown state must remain unknown, and inventory cannot grant authority.

decisions.question: How will efficiency and usability claims be qualified?
decisions.choice: Preregister baseline/candidate cases, host identities, actual usage/time/quality thresholds and human questions before evaluation. Evaluate retained successful and failed runs; unavailable accounting or people keep required measurements blocked.
alternatives: Infer savings from stdout bytes or command counts
Use only successful pairs or agent-simulated humans
Compress all language or history unconditionally
decisions.rationale: Total outcome cost and incorrect acceptance determine system value. Existing evidence does not prove savings; controlled language and fewer calls are hypotheses to test.
